questions.claim: Richard Dawkins said: "We are going to die, and that makes us the lucky ones"
bell hooks said: "Feminism is a movement to end sexism, sexist exploitation, and oppression"
Morgan Freeman said “Black history is American history” in his 2005 interview with Mike Wallace.
Samuel Beckett wrote Estragon’s opening line “Nothing to be done” in Waiting for Godot.
Anthony Bourdain said: "Your body is not a temple, it's an amusement park. Enjoy the ride"
Calvin Coolidge said: "I do not choose to run for President in 1928"
The historical Mao Zedong said “The real war is within us. History is a symptom of our disease.”
James Joyce originated the saying about actions being interpreters of thoughts.
The familiar two-sentence maxim is the exact wording of Margaret Atwood’s original account.
James Joyce wrote the two sentences beginning “I am tomorrow.”
Joseph Heller wrote “The end result of experiencing terror and injury is not an increase in compassion, but a tendency toward callousness.” in Catch-22.
Jean Piaget wrote the exact popular wording “When you teach a child something you take away forever his chance of discovering it for himself.”
Mao Zedong gave the reply “It’s too early to tell” when asked about the French Revolution.
Jiddu Krishnamurti said these exact words: It is no measure of health to be well-adjusted to a profoundly sick society.
Teresa of Ávila said or wrote the exact English saying “Pain is never permanent.”
George Bernard Shaw wrote “Life isn’t about finding yourself. Life is about creating yourself.”
Nikita Khrushchev made the circulating statement: We will take America without firing a shot. We do not have to invade the U.S. We will destroy you from within.
George R. R. Martin said: Art is not a democracy. People don't get to vote on how it ends.
